==English==
[[File:Light switch inside.jpg|thumb|right|A light '''switch'''.]]
[[File:D-Link DES-1024D.jpg|thumb|A networking '''switch'''.]]

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:bor<unc>|dum:swijch}}
Perhaps from {{bor|en|dum|swijch||[[twig]]}}, {{etydate|c|1592|nocap=1}}. The ''mechanical device for altering the direction of something'' sense is {{etydate|c|1797|nocap=1}}, pertaining to pivoted rails on minecart railways,<ref>Oxford English Dictionary, s.v. “switch (n.), sense I.3.a,” June 2024, https://doi.org/10.1093/OED/4056072461.</ref> which were once wooden.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|swĭch}}
* {{IPA|en|/swɪt͡ʃ/|a=RP,GA,CA,AU}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-switch.ogg|a=US}}
* {{IPA|en|/swət͡ʃ/|a=NZ}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɪtʃ|s=1}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{senseid|en|Q5320}} A [[device]] to turn [[electric]] [[current]] [[turn on|on]] and [[turn off|off]] or direct its [[flow]].
# A [[change]] or [[exchange]].
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=07 Dec 85|volume=13|number=21|journal=Gay Community News|page=15|author=Nicholas Deutsch|title=Epstein on the Beach (review)|text=After many complications and sudden '''switches''' of career and identity for all {{...}} they end up selling out for fame and money, and leave the boardwalk for good.}}
#* {{quote-web|en
|date=January 19, 2011
|author=Jonathan Stevenson
|title=Leeds 1 - 3 Arsenal
|work=w:BBC Sport
|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/fa_cup/9364559.stm
|page=
|passage=Wenger sent on {{w|Cesc Fabregas}} and {{w|Robin Van Persie|Van Persie}} to try to finish Leeds off and with 14 minutes left the '''switch''' paid off as the Spaniard sent {{w|Nicklas Bendtner|Bendtner}} away down the right and his wonderful curling cross was headed in by Van Persie at the far post.
|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120323041021/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/fa_cup/9364559.stm}}
# {{lb|en|rail transport|US|Philippines}} A movable section of [[railroad]] [[track]] which allows the train to be directed down one of two destination tracks; (set of) [[points]].
# A long, slender woody plant stem or a flexible, thin rod used as a [[whip]] to administer [[corporal punishment]] in the United States.
#* {{RQ:Baldwin Mountain|year_published=2001|chapter=Florence's Prayer|passage=Their mother would walk out into the yard and cut a '''switch''' from a tree and beat him—beat him, it seemed to Florence, until any other boy would have fallen down dead; {{...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2007|author=Jeffrey W. Hamilton|title=Raising Godly Children in a Wicked World|page=15|publisher=Lulu.com
|passage="A proper '''switch''' is a slim, flexible branch off a tree or a bush. A switch applied to the buttocks stings fiercely. It may leave red marks or bruises, but it causes no lasting damage.."}}
# {{lb|en|musical instruments}} {{synonym of|en|rute}}.
# {{lb|en|computer science}} A [[CLI|command line]] notation allowing specification of optional behavior.
#: {{ux|en|Use the /b '''switch''' to specify black-and-white printing.}}
# {{lb|en|computing|programming}} A [[programming]] [[construct]] that takes different actions depending on the [[value]] of an [[expression]].
# {{lb|en|computing|networking}} A networking device connecting multiple wires, allowing them to communicate simultaneously, when possible. Compare to the less efficient [[hub]] device that solely duplicates network packets to each wire.
# {{lb|en|telecommunication}} A system of specialized [[relay]]s, computer hardware, or other equipment which allows the interconnection of a calling party's telephone line with any called party's line.
# {{lb|en|genetics}} A mechanism within [[DNA]] that activates or deactivates a [[gene]].
# {{lb|en|especially|BDSM}} One who is [[willing]] to take either a [[submissive]] or a [[dominant]] [[role]] in a [[sexual]] [[relationship]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2012|author=Terri-Jean Bedford|title=Bondage Bungalow Fantasies|page=99
|passage=Ideally, if one of your ladies happens to be a '''switch''' (or would be willing to switch for this scene), I would love to be able to inflict a little "revenge tickling" as well, as part of a scenario.}}
# {{lb|en|historical}} A separate mass or [[tress]] of [[hair]], or of some substance (such as [[jute]]) made to resemble hair, formerly worn on the head by women.
# {{lb|en|card games|uncountable}} A variant of [[crazy eights]] where one card, such as an ace, reverses the direction of play.
# {{lb|en|firearms|slang}} {{synonym of|en|Glock switch}}.
## {{lb|en|slang|metonym}} A [[Glock]] pistol equipped with a [[Glock switch]].
# {{lb|en|sports}} A play in which the ball (or equivalent) is moved from one side of the playing area to the other.
#* {{quote-journal|en|title=How the Brisbane Lions are switching directions in the AFL to achieve attacking success|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2023-07-20/afl-brisbane-lions-switching-directions-for-attacking-success/102620726|work={{w|ABC News (Australia)|ABC News}}|location=Sydney|last1=Atkinson|first1=Cody|last2=Lawson|first2=Sean|date=20 July 2023|accessdate=27 May 2025|text=Once a sign of surrender and lead protection, the backwards kick plays a role in one of the most enterprising, enjoyable phases of the modern game: the '''switch'''. In an era where zones, presses, zone-presses and floods are ever present, the '''switch''' breaks through these tactical innovations like a hot knife through butter.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230801133636/https://www.abc.net.au/news/2023-07-20/afl-brisbane-lions-switching-directions-for-attacking-success/102620726}}
# {{lb|en|[[multiplicity]] [[slang]]}} The process of the currently [[front]]ing [[headmate]] changing; an instance of this.
#: {{ux|en|'''Switches''' only happen once every couple weeks for us, but they're quite sudden when they happen.}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[exchange]].
#: {{ux|en|I want to '''switch''' this red dress for a green one.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-01|volume=407|issue=8838
|page=13 (Technology Quarterly)
|url=http://www.economist.com/news/technology-quarterly/21578516-transport-new-train-technologies-are-less-visible-and-spread-less-quickly|title=Ideas coming down the track
|passage=A “moving platform” scheme{{...}}is more technologically ambitious than maglev trains even though it relies on conventional rails. Local trains would use side-by-side rails to roll alongside intercity trains and allow passengers to '''switch''' trains by stepping through docking bays.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130713175015/http://www.economist.com/news/technology-quarterly/21578516-transport-new-train-technologies-are-less-visible-and-spread-less-quickly}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To change (something) to the specified [[state]] using a switch.
#: {{ux|en|'''Switch''' the light on.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-01|volume=407|issue=8838
|page=13 (Technology Quarterly)
|url=http://www.economist.com/news/technology-quarterly/21578516-transport-new-train-technologies-are-less-visible-and-spread-less-quickly|title=Ideas coming down the track
|passage=When '''switched''' on, air brakes activate car by car, from the locomotive to the back of the train.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130713175015/http://www.economist.com/news/technology-quarterly/21578516-transport-new-train-technologies-are-less-visible-and-spread-less-quickly}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|in modern times Southern US}} To [[whip]] or [[hit]] with a switch.
#* {{RQ:Conrad Heart of Darkness|part=II|passage=They were looking on the ground, absorbed in thought. The manager was '''switching''' his leg with a slender twig: his sagacious relative lifted his head.}}
#* {{quote-book|en |author={{w|Dorothy M. Johnson}}|year=1950|newversion=in |type2=book |editor2=|title=Flame on the Frontier|title2=Indian Country|location2=London |publisher2=Corgi|year2=1961 |page2=11|text="Am I going to have to '''switch''' you?"}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[change]] [[place]]s, [[task]]s, etc.
#: {{ux|en|I want to '''switch''' to a different seat.}}
# {{lb|en|slang|intransitive}} To get [[angry]] [[suddenly]]; to [[quickly]] or [[unreasonably]] become [[enraged]].
# To swing or whisk.
#: ''to '''switch''' a cane''
# To be swung or whisked.
#: {{ux|en|The angry cat's tail '''switched''' back and forth.}}
# To [[trim]].
# To turn from one railway track to another; to transfer by a switch; generally with ''off'', ''from'', etc.
#: ''to '''switch''' off a train; to '''switch''' a car from one track to another''
# {{lb|en|ecclesiastical}} To shift to another [[circuit]].
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[take on]] the opposite role ([[leader]] vs. [[follower]]) in a [[partner dance]].
# {{lb|en|sports|transitive}} To move (the ball or equivalent) from one side of the playing area to the other.
